name: TRACE (Trust, Runtime Attestation and Compliance Evidence)
status: Specification version 0.2, described in its text as "0.2: Draft" with status "RFC: Request for Comments"; the repository README calls it a Developer Preview launched on 23 June 2026, and the Python package agentrust-trace 0.11.0 was released on 2026-09-25. The README states that the specification is hosted at the Linux Foundation as "TRACE Specification, a Series of LF Projects, LLC", and a Linux Foundation press release of 2026-08-25 announces the contribution of TRACE from OPAQUE. Reading of 2026-10-13: the README of the repository now says "a proposal to bring it into the Agentic AI Foundation as a Sandbox project is in progress" and points to aaif/project-proposals issue #42, which is open with the label Under Review, 8 comments and a last update on 2026-10-02; the specification stays at v0.2 ("Spec v0.2 is current"), main is at commit 8562b09 (2026-10-13, 00:33 UTC), and the latest release objects are conformance-v0.6.2 (2026-10-03, the conformance test package) and v0.11.0 (2026-09-25, the Python package agentrust-trace 0.11.0, numbered apart from the specification). The folder spec/ also holds a draft named mcp-profile-v0.3-draft.md, not read. Reading of 2026-10-21: the README still says "Spec v0.2 is current" and still describes the AAIF Sandbox proposal as "in progress"; issue #42 is open, labelled Under Review, with 9 comments and a last update on 2026-10-15. In its last comment (2026-10-15) the filer, the project lead of TRACE, writes that the contributing entity is now "TRACE Specification, a Series of LF Projects, LLC" and that "OPAQUE Systems wound down on 12 October"; he also repeats a question of 2026-09-21 about a Technical Committee sponsor, and the issue shows no reply to it. These statements are the filer's own; no AAIF decision was read. MAINTAINERS.md now lists the Project Lead, two repository maintainers and two reviewers (since 2026-10-15); the two OPAQUE spec editors read on 2026-10-09 are no longer listed.
relevance: The specification says "This is the rulebook for TRACE: it defines the Trust Record (a signed receipt describing one AI agent run), how records are anchored in a" The README describes TRACE as "an open format for a signed receipt of an AI agent run: what ran, where, under which rules, on what kind of data, and which" and states its limit: "A v0.2 signature proves who made a record and that it has not changed. It does not prove the hardware claims inside it". The specification text is under the Community Specification License 1.0 and the code under Apache 2.0 (LICENSE and README); GitHub's repository metadata reports the licence as NOASSERTION. MAINTAINERS.md lists as Project Lead Imran Siddique (AgenTrust-io), as spec editors Rishabh Poddar and Aaron Fulkerson (OPAQUE Systems), and two repository maintainers listed in the same file. The Linux Foundation press release says "The Linux Foundation will provide vendor-neutral governance for TRACE to support sustainability and long-term growth." In the AAIF Identity and Trust work TRACE is the format cited by the shared runner of agentrust-io/integrations, which validates "reference shapes" of the released package agentrust-trace 0.11.0, a reference package, not a version of the specification, which is v0.2 (see aaif-identity-trust).

evidence.read: On 2026-10-26: the release list of trace-spec (tag names, release titles, dates) and the README line "Spec v0.2 is current" (gh).
evidence.not_read: The rest of the specification (980 lines), the schema, the conformance suite, the roadmap and governance files, the limitations file.
